native_result.query: In which century did summed social capital peak, what individual social capital components like gold, monument etc increase?
native_result.HypoA: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?
native_result.HypoB: Summed social capital (equal-weighted z-score sum of copper-and-gold, amber, and monument count on 100-year bins) peaked in the 14th century BCE (1400 BCE bin, index 4.238; the 1300 BCE bin ties it, forming a 1400-1300 BCE plateau in the Old Bronze Age). The components increasing into the peak are copper-and-gold (z -0.36 at 1500 BCE to +2.54 at 1400 BCE) and monument count (0.17 to 1.71), with amber rising only marginally in the final step (-0.61 to -0.01, after climbing from -1.07 at 1800 BCE). Note that 'gold' is only available combined with copper in the data (CopperGold/ZCU_AU column), and including monument size in the index does not change the peak (4.904 at 1400 BCE).
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/capital.csv (decimal-comma format; dropped group/color columns); verified it matches the 37 overlapping 100-yr bins of time_series_data.csv exactly (max abs diff 0.0) and extends 2 bins earlier; computed the equal-weighted sum of z-scores ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument over the 39 bins; located the argmax (1400 BCE, tied with 1300 BCE); extracted the 6-bin pre-peak trajectory (1800-1400 BCE) and classified each component by 200- and 400-year changes; ran a sensitivity index including ZMW (MonumentSize), which peaks at the same 1400 BCE bin. Executed script: analysis.py; full index table: summed_social_capital_index.csv.

sub_hypo.text: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monument Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneously while summer social capital peaks.
sub_hypo.relations: Monument Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneously, coinciding with a peak in summer social capital. No corresponding column for summer social capital is specified.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?

sub_hypo.text: Summed social capital peaks at 1400 BCE with an index of 4.238, tied with 1300 BCE, forming a 1400–1300 BCE plateau in the Old Bronze Age.
sub_hypo.context: Archaeological capital data across 39 100-year bins; the peak plateau occurs in the Old Bronze Age.
sub_hypo.relations: The equal-weighted sum ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument reaches its maximum of 4.238 at both 1400 and 1300 BCE. Copper and gold are measured jointly, not separately.

sub_hypo.text: Copper-and-gold and monument count increase into the social-capital peak, while amber rises only marginally in the final step after an earlier climb.
sub_hypo.context: The pre-peak trajectory from 1800 to 1400 BCE in 100-year bins, particularly the final step from 1500 to 1400 BCE.
sub_hypo.relations: From 1500 to 1400 BCE, copper-and-gold increases from -0.36 to 2.54 and monument count from 0.17 to 1.71; amber increases from -0.61 to -0.01, after rising from -1.07 at 1800 BCE. These components contribute equally by weight to the summed index.

sub_hypo.text: Including monument size in the social-capital index does not change the 1400 BCE peak, where the expanded index equals 4.904.
sub_hypo.context: Sensitivity analysis of archaeological capital data across the same 39 100-year bins.
sub_hypo.relations: Adding monument size (ZMW) to ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument preserves the peak at 1400 BCE, with an expanded index value of 4.904.

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Summed social capital (equal-weighted z-score sum of copper-and-gold, amber, and monument count on 100-year bins) peaked in the 14th century BCE (1400 BCE bin, index 4.238; the 1300 BCE bin ties it, forming a 1400-1300 BCE plateau in the Old Bronze Age). The components increasing into the peak are copper-and-gold (z -0.36 at 1500 BCE to +2.54 at 1400 BCE) and monument count (0.17 to 1.71), with amber rising only marginally in the final step (-0.61 to -0.01, after climbing from -1.07 at 1800 BCE). Note that 'gold' is only available combined with copper in the data (CopperGold/ZCU_AU column), and including monument size in the index does not change the peak (4.904 at 1400 BCE).
